text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty triggered for dedicated pool gamma-prod-usw2. Condition: sustained request_queue_depth > 400 for 2m and error_rate > 0.5%. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/gamma-capacity

Anne (oncall): ack'd on PagerDuty, I'm on it. Starting quick triage — pulling dashboards and logs.

PagerDuty: Alert acknowledged by Anne (oncall) at 1834510000

MattR: p95 climbed to ~1.7s, p99 ~3.4s, spikes coincident with enqueue backlog. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/d/cluster/gamma-prod-usw2

Jess (infra): FYI I see an infra change earlier — autoscale min_instances lowered from 2 -> 1 as part of a cost experiment at 02:13 UTC (commit abc123). Could explain sudden capacity drop.

Anne (oncall): hmm. If we dropped the min pool size during peak region, that explains burst starvation. I'm going to temporarily force min=2 and enable emergency burst. Commands:
```
redwoodctl pools set-autoscale --pool gamma-prod-usw2 --min-instances 2 --reason "oncall emergency"
redwoodctl pools burst-enable --pool gamma-prod-usw2 --units gpu --amount 1 --duration 15m
```

Kumar (infra-sre): executing burst-enable, adding +1 GPU. Job id burst-2026-17. ETA ~40s to provision.

MattR: queue depth starts dropping after burst. Seeing about 60% reduction in queued requests in the first minute. Still seeing isolated 500s from worker-4.

Anne (oncall): collecting worker logs for worker-4.

Logs from worker-4:
```
[2026-03-14T03:18:22Z] ERROR Alloc failed: cannot allocate 1.2GB for kv_cache
[2026-03-14T03:18:22Z] WARN evicting prefixes
[2026-03-14T03:18:23Z] INFO request=aa12 handler=generate latency=3200ms status=500
```

Jess (infra): that looks like node-level memory pressure. I'll schedule a graceful restart of worker-4 and disable kv_cache prefetch on it to avoid immediate OOMs.

Commands run:
```
redwoodctl nodes restart --node worker-4 --graceful
redwoodctl config set --node worker-4 kv_cache_prefetch=false
```

Kumar (infra-sre): restart in progress for worker-4. Rejoin expected ~90s.

MattR: after restart, worker-4 rejoined healthy. 5xx rate back under 0.1%. p95 stabilized ~1.0s. queue depth ~110.

Anne (oncall): as a protective measure, I'm doing a targeted routing shift: non-SLO/free-tier traffic -> fallback-small pool to reduce stress while we observe. Using internal routing API with tenant filter.

Dana (acct): notifying Gamma customer team and CS. Sending initial customer note: brief outage window, mitigation in progress, follow-up RCA forthcoming. Customer impact estimated: degraded latency for some free tier requests for ~8-12 minutes.

PagerDuty: Incident annotated: burst capacity added, node restart performed, routing adjusted. Mitigations acknowledged by Anne at 1834510070.

Jess (infra): created follow-up ticket INC-2026-433: actions: revert autoscale experiment for reserved pools, add autoscale change guardrails, add node mem >85% alert, extend default burst duration for dedicated clusters to 2m, add pre-deploy canary for autoscale changes.

Anne (oncall): plan to monitor 30m then hand to night oncall (Jess) if stable. Scheduling postmortem with infra and product. Handoff ETA 1834510500.

Kumar (infra-sre): added ephemeral metric alert: any single-node mem >85% for >60s -> page infra-sre. Also added audit rule to detect autoscale min changes in prod reserved pools.

Anne (oncall): closing active pager; incident state: mitigated, monitoring. Short summary: root cause = autoscale min reduced during cost test + node-level memory regression on worker-4. Impact = transient queueing and higher latency for non-SLO traffic. Mitigations = forced min instances, burst capacity, restart bad node, fallback routing. Follow-ups = INC-2026-433, postmortem scheduled.

MattR: nice work, smooth run. :thumbsup:

Participants: Incident Bot, PagerDuty, Anne (oncall), MattR, Jess (infra), Kumar (infra-sre), Dana (acct)
